clue.text: Very unusual baby seen in outbuilding, OK? It was reckoned the longest day

definitions.text: It was reckoned the longest day

parts.note: a barn is a farm outbuilding

indicators.note: something very unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters of baby are rearranged

parts.note: right, as in 'all right', means OK

explanation.surface: A nativity-style scene: a remarkable infant found in a shed, with someone checking all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Bright is the old name for St Barnabas's Day, 11 June, which under the Julian calendar fell near the summer solstice: 'Barnaby bright, the longest day and the shortest night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the calendar reform of 1752, St Barnabas's Day was traditionally held to be the year's longest day, hence the rhyme.

clue.text: Painted brown restaurant red instead of half rose

indicators.note: red is put in the place that half of rose occupied, a straight swap of one piece for another

parts.note: a bistro is a small restaurant
the first half of the word rose
taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant repainted, its colours changed from rose to red and brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Bistre is a brown pigment made from soot, so bistred means coloured with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a dark brown pigment, so something bistred has been coloured or washed brown with it.

clue.text: Town in Nevada, whopper going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a oner is something outstanding, a whopper

explanation.surface: A tall tale told in a Nevada town getting bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno is a city in the US state of Nevada, famous for casinos and quick divorces.

clue.text: Cast in plays responding to stimulus in unexpected direction?

definitions.text: responding to stimulus in unexpected direction?

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Actors in shows reacting in unexpected ways to a director's prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast in plays' reads as theatre, but cast in is the material and plays the signal. A nastic movement in a plant is a response not directed by where the stimulus comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call a plant movement nastic when its direction is independent of the stimulus, as when petals open in warmth.

clue.text: Impressive performance? Something uplifting seen in French Academy

parts.note: a bra lifts and supports
vu is French for seen
RA is the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A show admired at the Académie française.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Academy' looks like one institution, but French goes with seen and Academy stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravura is a brilliant, showy display of skill, especially in music.

clue.text: 'Youth as of old lost love' — as might be said pulling on a Capstan?

definitions.text: as might be said pulling on a Capstan?

indicators.note: lost means these letters go missing from the word

parts.note: ut is Latin for as, and Latin is the language of old
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A wistful old saying about youth and a lost sweetheart, murmured over a Capstan cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Capstan looks like the cigarette brand, but it is the ship's winch that sailors heaved round while chanting. The quoted phrase is pure instruction, not a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Yo-ho is the rhythmic cry sailors chanted while hauling ropes or turning a capstan together.

clue.text: Tart nervous about close relationships, angrier than the rest

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the other piece
nervous suggests jittery and unsettled, so the letters of tart are jumbled

parts.note: ties are close bonds between people

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued, anxious person getting crosser than everyone about their intimate relationships.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty means irritable or bad-tempered, and this is its superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal for irritable, so the rattiest is the most irritable of a group.

clue.text: Plant genus from SA, one by one beginning to adapt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
x, the multiplication sign, is read as by, as in two by four
I again, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of adapt

explanation.surface: A South African plant adapting one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South Africa, where these corn lilies grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ixia is a genus of South African corm-forming plants of the iris family, the corn lilies.

clue.text: Cooked dish set before one containing nothing heavy

indicators.note: the combined pieces hold the next letter inside them
the first piece is placed ahead of the next one

parts.note: a grill is a dish of grilled food
a means one
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A meal put in front of someone, empty of anything stodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy' looks like a description of food; it is the noun for a thug or bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy is a hired thug or minder, and gorilla is slang for exactly the same kind of muscle.

clue.text: It may be dished out for Ebor dasher

definitions.text: It may be dished out for Ebor dasher

indicators.note: dishing out scatters things, so the letters of the two words are served up in a new order

explanation.surface: Food served to a racehorse running in the Ebor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ebor is a big flat race at York, so an Ebor dasher is a racehorse, and the whole clue describes its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse bread was a coarse loaf of beans and bran baked as feed for horses.

clue.text: Empty, quite empty? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, the answer lying within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of quite and the start of the second empty

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a thing is completely void and being told it is not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: Teem usually means to pour or swarm, but it also has an old sense of to empty or pour out.
explanation.definitionFit: Teem can mean to pour out or discharge the contents of a vessel, the same act as emptying it.

clue.text: Bridge defence contrived by pair once in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A card-table partnership devising a defence once things went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests the card game, but it is the structure over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice apron is a wedge-shaped structure upstream of a bridge pier that breaks up ice floes to protect the pier.

clue.text: Light brown facial mixed with water in — cosmetician's centrepiece (10, three words)

indicators.note: the word for water goes inside the jumbled letters
the letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: the middle letter of cosmetician
eau is French for water, also used in English

explanation.surface: A beautician blending a face treatment with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Café au lait, coffee with milk, names the pale brown colour of that drink.

clue.text: What e.g. Moroccan musician plays in bar, French one?

parts.note: bar meaning without is sans in French
a means one

explanation.surface: A North African musician performing in a French bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it is the preposition meaning except. Morocco is just an example of an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: A sansa is an African thumb piano with metal tongues on a board, also called a mbira or kalimba.

clue.text: Probable misprint in Shakespeare was exciting (well, almost)

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: stirred means roused or excited

explanation.surface: A probable typo in a Shakespeare text was rather thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed takes rare words from Chambers, which records some words found only in Shakespeare's early printed texts as probable misprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists a few obscure forms from Shakespeare's early printed texts as likely printer's errors rather than genuine words.

clue.text: Ruck: scrum's first on spot, let loose

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter sits on top of what follows
the first letter of scrum

parts.note: the first letter of scrum
quat is a Shakespearean word for a pimple or spot

indicators.note: letting loose frees the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby ruck: the scrum half arriving on the spot and the ball let loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruck' looks like the rugby term, but it is the dialect verb meaning to squat or crouch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruck in dialect is to squat or crouch down, which is what squattle means.

clue.text: Small volume I'm at's reworked branch of electricity

parts.note: vol is the short form of volume

indicators.note: reworked letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reworking a little book into a study of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaism is the old name for current electricity from chemical action, after Volta, also called galvanism.

clue.text: More liqueurs will drown this reminder of things past

indicators.note: the answer is submerged within the run of letters, as if drowned in the drinks

parts.note: the letters run from the end of more into the start of liqueurs

explanation.surface: Another round of after-dinner drinks will blot out a memento of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Relique is the archaic spelling of relic, an object kept in memory of a person or time.

clue.text: Distinctive pods people put in pot, often copper

indicators.note: the one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lota is an Indian water pot, usually of brass or copper
men means people

explanation.surface: People dropping pods into a copper cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A loment is a type of seed pod constricted between seeds that breaks into one-seeded joints; the Latin plural is lomenta.

clue.text: Record's climbing — about fifth in charts — dizzying climb?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about the next letter
in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an elpee is an LP record, so record's gives elpee's
the fifth letter of charts

explanation.surface: A single rising up the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Elpee is the spelt-out form of LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a tall church spire, and scaling one, as steeplejacks do, is a vertigo-inducing ascent.

clue.text: Distinctive group of cells is rented out

parts.note: a property that is let is rented to a tenant

explanation.surface: A prison block of cells being let to tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: Cells here are biological, as in the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy an islet is a small isolated cluster of cells, such as the insulin-producing islets of the pancreas.

clue.text: Entangle translator with headword that's come up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lemma is a dictionary headword

explanation.surface: A translator getting tangled up with a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hamper or entangle, from the trammel net that snares fish or birds.

clue.text: Assistant barmen in Dublin copper thinks highly of

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate someone is to esteem them

explanation.surface: A Dublin policeman admires the pub staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal. In Ireland a barman's assistant is called a curate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish usage a curate is an assistant barman, a joking borrowing of the clergyman's title.

clue.text: Last pair in makes runs switching to chase as before?

indicators.note: the final two letters of the word are the ones affected, like the last batting pair
the two letters change places

parts.note: in cricket, making runs is scoring them

explanation.surface: A cricket tail-end partnership piling on runs while chasing a target.
explanation.walkthrough: Scorse is Spenser's word, so 'as before' marks it as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used scorse to mean to chase or pursue, an obsolete sense recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Lament head of KGB appearing in Russian parliament

indicators.note: the letter shows up inside the other word

parts.note: the Duma is Russia's parliament

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of KGB

explanation.surface: A KGB chief turning up before the Russian legislature to grieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumka is a Slavonic folk ballad, a melancholy elegy or lament, used by Dvořák.

clue.text: Italian town, symbol of greenness, restricting blemish

indicators.note: the outer word confines the other within it

parts.note: the pea is the standard of green, as in pea-green
a scar is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: An Italian town, an emblem of eco-friendliness, keeps its flaw contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Pescara is a port city on Italy's Adriatic coast, capital of its province.

clue.text: Old inn sign one's task shifting in out of the wind?

parts.note: a is one, and 's stands for is

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

indicators.note: the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: An old pub sign being moved indoors out of the gale.
explanation.definitionFit: An alestake was a pole set up outside an alehouse as a sign that ale was sold there.

clue.text: Harrow, traditionally, wherein a girl's not succeeded finally

indicators.note: not marks a letter to be dropped from the word
the letter dropped is the one at the end

parts.note: lass means a girl

explanation.surface: At Harrow, the boys' school, a girl failed to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrow' suggests the school, but harrow is an old cry of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow was a medieval exclamation of grief or alarm, the same kind of cry as the interjection here.

clue.text: What Jock has on his chips, lightly fried for the most part?

definitions.text: What Jock has on his chips

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to cook food quickly in a little fat is the French-named cooking term

explanation.surface: A Scot's chips, mostly given a quick fry.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a Scot, and saut is Scots for salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Saut is the Scots form of salt, the seasoning sprinkled on chips.

clue.text: Peg, horse ridden by king

indicators.note: in a down clue the horse has its rider sitting on top

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A tethering peg for a horse with a king in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A knag is a knot in wood or a peg for hanging things on.

clue.text: Spring in northern parts? Blade's led by onset of venery

indicators.note: the following piece comes after this first one
the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of venery, an old word for hunting
an oar's blade, so blade is an oar; 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A spring season in the north, a blade leading the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Venery is hunting. Voar is the Orkney and Shetland word for spring.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orkney and Shetland dialect, voar is the spring season, the time of sowing.

clue.text: Like sheep having a bit of a kip in minor road?

indicators.note: the coin goes inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a minor road
the at is a hundredth of a kip, the currency of Laos

explanation.surface: Sheep taking a nap in a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kip' looks like a nap; it is Laos's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanate means woolly, covered with wool, as sheep are.

clue.text: Rowing boat, minute, including professionals and amateurs

parts.note: a proa is a Malay boat that may be rowed or sailed

explanation.surface: A small rowing boat crewed by experts and novices together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am event is one open to both professional and amateur competitors.

clue.text: Fence leap badly, stiff inside

indicators.note: the further letters sit inside the jumbled word
something done badly is botched, so the letters of leap are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram material, which as published is one I short of the letters needed
sad is used of bread or pastry that is heavy and stiff, having failed to rise

explanation.surface: A horse jumping a fence clumsily and coming down stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: As published, the clue supplies no I: leap jumbled and SAD for stiff give every other letter, so an I (perhaps a dropped word such as 'one') is missing from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes or pointed pales set side by side, used for defence or enclosure.

clue.text: Dutch parliament instals chief

parts.note: state has an old sense of to install or establish
general means chief, as in general manager

explanation.surface: The Netherlands parliament puts its leader in office.
explanation.definitionFit: The States General is the bicameral legislature of the Netherlands.
